teach.title: The number sets
text: Natural numbers: 1, 2, 3, … Whole numbers: 0, 1, 2, 3, … Integers: …, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, …
Rational numbers can be written as a fraction of two integers. That includes terminating decimals like 0.25 and repeating decimals like 0.333…
Irrational numbers cannot be written as a fraction. Their decimals never end and never repeat, like √2 and π. Rational and irrational numbers together make the real numbers.

steps: −6 is an integer, so it is also rational and real.
3/4 is a fraction of integers, so it is rational and real, but not an integer.
√5 is not a perfect square root, so it is irrational and real.

questions.hint: A square root of a non-perfect square never ends or repeats.
questions.solution: 0.25 = 1/4 and 22/7 are fractions, so they are rational. √16 = 4 is rational. √7 is not a perfect square root, so it is irrational.

questions.prompt: Which set of numbers contains 0 but does not contain −5?
questions.hint: Natural numbers start at 1. Which set has no negatives?
questions.solution: Natural numbers do not include 0. Integers and rational numbers both include −5. Whole numbers are 0, 1, 2, … so they include 0 but not −5.

questions.prompt: How many of these numbers are integers? 4, −7, 1/2, 0, 2.5
questions.hint: An integer has no fraction or decimal part.
questions.solution: 4, −7, and 0 are integers. 1/2 and 2.5 are not. That is 3 integers.

questions.hint: Can you write it as a fraction?
questions.solution: A repeating decimal can be written as a fraction. 0.333… = 1/3, so it is rational.

choices: an irrational number, because it has a root
a rational number, and an integer
questions.hint: Find the square root first.
questions.solution: √49 = 7. That is an integer, so it is also rational and real.

questions.prompt: How many of these are irrational? −√9, π, 0.5, 8/4, √2
questions.hint: Simplify any root or fraction first.
questions.solution: −√9 = −3, 0.5 = 1/2, and 8/4 = 2 are all rational. Only π and √2 are irrational. That is 2.

choices: Every rational number is an integer
Every irrational number is a whole number
Every integer is a rational number
questions.hint: Any integer n can be written as n/1.
questions.solution: An integer n equals n/1, so it is rational. The other statements fail: 1/2 is rational but not an integer, and no irrational number is whole or natural.

questions.prompt: How many whole numbers are greater than −3 and less than 4?
questions.hint: Whole numbers start at 0.
questions.solution: The whole numbers in that range are 0, 1, 2, 3. That is 4 numbers.

teach.title: Commutative and associative
text: Commutative: order does not matter. a + b = b + a and a · b = b · a.
Associative: grouping does not matter. (a + b) + c = a + (b + c) and (a · b) · c = a · (b · c).
Subtraction and division are not commutative: 5 − 3 is not 3 − 5.

steps: The numbers stay in the same order.
This is the associative property of multiplication.

teach.title: Distributive, identity, inverse
text: Distributive: a(b + c) = ab + ac.
Identity: a + 0 = a and a · 1 = a.
Inverse: a + (−a) = 0 and a · (1/a) = 1 for a ≠ 0.

steps: Adding 0 leaves the number the same.
This is the identity property of addition.

questions.hint: The order of the numbers changed.
questions.solution: The numbers swapped places. That is the commutative property.

questions.hint: The order is the same. What moved?
questions.solution: The parentheses moved but the order did not. That is the associative property.

questions.hint: 6 is multiplied by each term inside the parentheses.
questions.solution: 6 multiplies both x and 4. That is the distributive property.

questions.hint: Adding 0 changes nothing.
questions.solution: 0 is the additive identity because adding it leaves the number unchanged.

questions.hint: The two numbers multiply to give 1.
questions.solution: 5 and 1/5 multiply to 1, the multiplicative identity. That is the inverse property.

questions.prompt: The identity property says a · __ = a. What number goes in the blank?
questions.hint: Which number leaves a unchanged when you multiply?
questions.solution: Multiplying by 1 leaves a unchanged, so the blank is 1.

questions.hint: A number plus its opposite gives what?
questions.solution: −8 and 8 are opposites. Their sum is 0. That is the additive inverse property.

questions.prompt: Which equation is NOT true for all numbers?
questions.hint: Try small numbers such as a = 5, b = 3.
questions.solution: Subtraction is not commutative. 5 − 3 = 2 but 3 − 5 = −2. The other three equations are always true.

teach.title: Using properties to simplify
text: Properties can make a calculation easier. Group numbers that make 10, 100, or other round numbers.
The distributive property also works backward: ab + ac = a(b + c).

teach.title: Opposites and reciprocals
text: The additive inverse of a is −a.
The multiplicative inverse (reciprocal) of a/b is b/a. Flip the fraction and keep the sign.

questions.prompt: Which property lets you rewrite 4 · (25 · 7) as (4 · 25) · 7 so you can do 100 · 7?
questions.hint: The numbers stay in order. Only the parentheses move.
questions.solution: Moving the parentheses is the associative property.

questions.hint: Distribute the 6 across 100 − 2.
The two terms traded places.
questions.solution: The terms swapped places, so this is the commutative property of addition.

questions.hint: Additive inverses add to 0.
questions.solution: 3/4 + (−3/4) = 0. The other pairs do not add to 0.

questions.prompt: What is the multiplicative inverse of −2/3? Type it as a fraction.
questions.hint: Flip the fraction and keep the sign.
5 is not spread over two terms here. The grouping changes.
questions.solution: The grouping changes from 5(2x) to (5 · 2)x. That is the associative property.

questions.prompt: 3 + (x + 7) = 3 + (7 + x) = (3 + 7) + x = 10 + x. Which properties are used, in order?
questions.hint: First the order of x and 7 flips. Then the grouping changes.
questions.solution: Step 1 swaps x and 7: commutative. Step 2 moves the parentheses: associative.

questions.prompt: Use the distributive property backward: 17 · 5 + 17 · 15 = 17(5 + 15). What is the value?
questions.hint: Add inside the parentheses first.

questions.prompt: A student writes 4(x − 3) = 4x − 3. What went wrong?
choices: The 4 was not multiplied by the 3
The commutative property was used wrongly
The 4 should be added to each term
questions.hint: Check whether 4 multiplies both terms.
questions.solution: The distributive property needs 4 · x and 4 · (−3). The right answer is 4x − 12.

teach.title: Mixing it together
text: Many problems combine ideas. Simplify any roots or fractions first, then name the set or the property.
A number can belong to several sets at once. Every integer is rational, and every rational number is real.

steps: 0 is not natural, since natural numbers start at 1.
0 is a whole number, an integer, a rational number (0/1), and a real number.

questions.hint: Simplify the root before deciding.
questions.solution: −√36 = −6, an integer, so it is rational. π, √20, and √0.5 never end or repeat.

questions.prompt: How many of these numbers are NOT integers? 0, −2, 5/3, √5, 1.25
questions.hint: Check each number for a fraction or decimal part.
questions.solution: 0 and −2 are integers. 5/3, √5, and 1.25 are not. That is 3.

questions.prompt: A number is real and rational but not an integer. Which could it be?
questions.hint: It must be a fraction that does not simplify to a whole number.
questions.solution: −5 and 0 are integers. √3 is irrational. 7/2 is rational but not an integer.

choices: Every whole number is an integer
Every natural number is a rational number
Every rational number is a real number
Every integer is a whole number
questions.hint: Try −2.
questions.solution: −2 is an integer but not a whole number, so the last statement, every integer is a whole number, is false. The others are true.

questions.prompt: Which equation does NOT use the commutative property?
questions.hint: Commutative means the order swaps.
questions.solution: Only 2(x + 1) = 2x + 2 spreads a factor over a sum. That is the distributive property.

questions.prompt: 12 + (−12) = 0 and (1/3) · 3 = 1 show which pair of properties?
questions.hint: Each pair of numbers combines to give an identity.
questions.solution: Opposites add to 0: additive inverse. Reciprocals multiply to 1: multiplicative inverse.

questions.hint: Distribute the 8 over 50 and 3.

questions.prompt: The number 0 belongs to which sets?
questions.hint: Natural numbers start at 1.
questions.solution: 0 is not natural. It is a whole number, an integer, a rational number (0/1), and a real number.

teach.title: Order of operations
text: Do operations in this order: grouping symbols, exponents, multiplication and division (left to right), then addition and subtraction (left to right).
Multiplication and division share a level, and so do addition and subtraction. Go left to right.

questions.hint: Multiply before you add.
Divide before you subtract.

questions.prompt: What is the first step in evaluating 2 + 3(4 − 1)²?
questions.hint: Grouping symbols come first.
questions.solution: Parentheses come first, so do 4 − 1 = 3. Then the exponent, then multiply, then add.

questions.hint: Do the parentheses, then multiply.
Exponent first, then multiply.
The exponent applies only to the 3, not to the negative sign.
questions.solution: −3² means −(3 · 3) = −9. Only (−3)² equals 9.

questions.hint: Exponent, then multiplication, then add and subtract left to right.
Multiplication and division go left to right.

teach.title: Negatives and absolute value
text: Treat (−3)² as −3 times −3 = 9. But −3² = −(3²) = −9.
Absolute value bars work like parentheses. Simplify inside first, then take the absolute value.
A fraction bar also groups. Work out the top and bottom separately, then divide.

questions.hint: Multiply first.
(−3)² means −3 times −3.
Simplify inside the second bars first.
The fraction bar groups the top and the bottom.
Work out the top and bottom separately.
Simplify inside the bars, then multiply.
Which one squares the negative sign too?
questions.solution: (−5)² = 25. The others all equal −25.

questions.hint: Parentheses, then the exponent, then multiply and divide left to right.

teach.title: Evaluating an expression
text: To evaluate, replace each variable with its value. Put the value in parentheses, especially if it is negative. Then follow the order of operations.

questions.hint: Replace x with 4.
Use parentheses around −3.
Square first, then apply the negative sign.
questions.solution: x² = 25. Then −25.

questions.hint: Replace a and b with parentheses.

questions.prompt: Evaluate (x + y)/(x − y) when x = 7 and y = 3.
questions.hint: The fraction bar groups top and bottom.

questions.prompt: Evaluate |m − n| when m = −2 and n = 6.
questions.hint: Subtract inside first, then take the absolute value.
Square first: (−2)² = 4.
Find each part separately.

questions.prompt: Convert to Fahrenheit with F = (9/5)C + 32 when C = −10.
questions.hint: Multiply (9/5) by −10 first.

teach.title: Nested grouping and mixed practice
text: With brackets inside brackets, work from the innermost pair outward.
Then substitute carefully and keep a clear order for every step.

questions.hint: Start with the innermost parentheses.

questions.prompt: Evaluate (3x − y²)/(2 − x) when x = 5 and y = −4.
questions.hint: Square y first: (−4)² = 16.

questions.prompt: Evaluate |2x − 3y| − x² when x = −2 and y = −1.
questions.hint: Work out the absolute value and the x² separately.
Parentheses, exponent, multiply, subtract.

questions.prompt: A student evaluates −3² + 4 and gets 13. What was the mistake?
questions.hint: What does the exponent apply to?
questions.solution: −3² = −9, so the answer is −9 + 4 = −5. The student used 9 instead of −9.

questions.prompt: Area of a trapezoid: A = (1/2)h(b₁ + b₂). Find A when h = 6, b₁ = 5, and b₂ = 9.
questions.hint: Add the bases first.

questions.prompt: Evaluate x² − 4xy + y² when x = 2 and y = −3.
questions.hint: Be careful with −4xy.
Square first: (−2)² = 4.

teach.title: Like terms
text: Terms are like terms when they have the same variable part with the same exponent. 5y and −2y are like. 3x and 3x² are not.
Combine like terms by adding their coefficients. The variable part stays the same.

questions.hint: Both the variable and the exponent must match.
questions.solution: 5y and −2y both have y to the first power. The other pairs differ in variable or exponent.

questions.prompt: In 4x² − 7x + 9, what is the coefficient of x?
questions.hint: The coefficient is the number multiplying the variable, including its sign.
questions.solution: The term with x is −7x, so the coefficient is −7.

questions.hint: Add the coefficients. Do the exponents change?
questions.solution: 5 + 3 = 8 and the variable part stays x. So 8x.

questions.hint: Combine the a terms, then the constants.
x² and x are not like terms.
questions.solution: 2x² + x² = 3x². The 3x has a different exponent, so it stays. 3x² + 3x.

questions.prompt: After simplifying 9x − 4x + 2x, what is the coefficient of x?
questions.solution: 9 − 4 + 2 = 7, so the result is 7x.

questions.prompt: Simplify 8n + 5 − 3n − 5. The answer is kn. What is k?
questions.hint: Do the constants cancel?
questions.solution: 8n − 3n = 5n and 5 − 5 = 0. So 5n, and k = 5.

questions.hint: Combine m terms with m terms and n terms with n terms.
questions.solution: 3m − m = 2m. 2n + 5n = 7n. So 2m + 7n.

teach.title: The distributive property
text: a(b + c) = ab + ac. Multiply the outside number by every term inside the parentheses.
Watch signs. A negative outside number flips the sign of every term inside.

questions.hint: Multiply 3 by both terms.
A negative times a negative is positive.

questions.prompt: Expand −4(3x + 2) to get ax + b. What is a + b?
questions.hint: Distribute −4 to both terms.
Half of 8x and half of 6.
Expand both groups, then combine.

questions.prompt: 2(3x + 1) + 5x simplifies to kx + 2. What is k?
questions.hint: Expand first: 6x + 2 + 5x.
The minus sign in front means multiply by −1.
Expand, then combine the x terms.

questions.prompt: Simplify 7(a + 2) − 7a. What number do you get?
questions.hint: Expand and look at the a terms.

teach.title: Subtracting a group
text: A minus sign in front of parentheses means multiply the group by −1. Every sign inside flips.
So (a + b) − (c − d) = a + b − c + d.

questions.hint: The minus sign applies to both terms in the group.
Subtracting −3 adds 3.

questions.prompt: (9x − 1) − (4x + 6) simplifies to kx − 7. What is k?
questions.hint: Subtract both terms of the second group.
The −6 inside becomes +6.

questions.prompt: A student simplifies (7x + 5) − (3x − 2) and gets 4x + 3. What was the mistake?
choices: The minus was not applied to the −2
The x terms were added instead of subtracted
questions.hint: Redo it carefully and compare the constants.
questions.solution: The correct work is 7x + 5 − 3x + 2 = 4x + 7. The student left −2 as −2 instead of +2.

questions.prompt: 3(x + 4) − 2(x − 5) simplifies to x + c. What is c?
questions.hint: Expand both products. Then subtract.
Expand 2(3x − 1) first, then subtract the group.
Distribute each minus separately.

questions.prompt: Subtract (x² + 2x) from (3x² − x). The result is ax² + bx. What is a + b?
questions.hint: Write it as (3x² − x) − (x² + 2x).
questions.solution: 3x² − x − x² − 2x = 2x² − 3x. So a = 2 and b = −3, and a + b = −1.

teach.title: Perimeter expressions
text: Perimeter is the sum of all the side lengths. Write the sides as expressions, add them, and combine like terms.
A rectangle with length L and width W has perimeter 2L + 2W.

example.problem: A triangle has sides x + 4, 2x − 1, and 3x + 2. Find the perimeter.

questions.prompt: A rectangle has length 2x + 3 and width x − 1. What is its perimeter?
questions.hint: Use P = 2L + 2W.

questions.prompt: A triangle has sides x + 4, 2x − 1, and 3x + 2. What is its perimeter?
questions.hint: Add all three sides.

questions.prompt: A square has side 3x − 2. Find its perimeter when x = 5.
questions.hint: The perimeter is 4 times the side.
questions.solution: Perimeter = 4(3x − 2) = 12x − 8. When x = 5, that is 60 − 8 = 52.

questions.prompt: A rectangle has width x + 2 and perimeter 8x + 4. What is its length?
questions.hint: Half the perimeter is length plus width.
questions.solution: Half of 8x + 4 is 4x + 2. Length = 4x + 2 − (x + 2) = 3x.

questions.hint: Expand both groups, then combine.

questions.prompt: 5 − 2(x − 3) + 3x simplifies to x + c. What is c?
questions.hint: Expand −2(x − 3) carefully.
Watch the sign on −3 · (−b).
Simplify first, then substitute.

teach.title: Undo operations in reverse
text: To solve an equation, get the variable alone. Undo operations with their opposites, doing the same thing to both sides.
If there are parentheses, distribute first. Then combine like terms, then undo adding or subtracting, then undo multiplying or dividing.

questions.hint: Subtract 7 from both sides first.
Add 9 to both sides.
Distribute the 2 first, or divide both sides by 2.

questions.prompt: What is a correct first step for solving 3x + 5 = 20?
questions.hint: Undo the addition first.
questions.solution: The 5 is added to 3x. Subtract 5 from both sides to get 3x = 15.

questions.hint: Combine the x terms first.
Subtract 4, then divide by −3.
Distribute, combine, then undo.
Solve, or test each answer.

teach.title: Variables on both sides
text: Move the variable terms to one side by adding or subtracting. Then solve as usual.
Pick the side that keeps the coefficient positive if you can. It avoids sign errors.

questions.hint: Subtract 3x from both sides.
Get the x terms on one side.
Add 3x to both sides.
Distribute the 3 first.
Subtract 6x, then add 7.
Distribute on both sides.
Distribute −2 across the group.
Distribute −2 carefully: −2 · −1 = +2.

teach.title: Clearing fractions and decimals
text: To clear fractions, multiply every term by the common denominator. To clear decimals, multiply every term by a power of 10.
Multiply every term, not just one side of the first term.

steps: The common denominator is 6. Multiply every term by 6: 3x + 2x = 60.

questions.hint: Subtract 2, then multiply by 3.
Multiply by the reciprocal, 3/2.
Multiply every term by 6.
Subtract 1.2 first.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest power of 10 that clears all decimals in 0.3x + 1.25 = 4.1?
questions.hint: 1.25 has two decimal places.
questions.solution: 1.25 needs two places, so multiply by 100: 30x + 125 = 410.

questions.hint: Cross-multiply or multiply by 12.
Subtract 0.3x from both sides.
Multiply every term by 4, including the 1/2.

teach.title: No solution and all real numbers
text: If the variables cancel and the result is false, like 3 = 8, there is no solution.
If the variables cancel and the result is true, like 7 = 7, every real number is a solution.
If a variable stays, you get one solution.

steps: This is always true, so all real numbers are solutions.

questions.hint: Distribute, then see what is left after you subtract 2x.
questions.solution: 2x + 6 = 2x + 6 gives 6 = 6, always true. All real numbers.

questions.hint: Subtract 3x from both sides.
questions.solution: 4 = −1 is false, so there is no solution.

questions.hint: Expand both products, then combine.
Distribute on the right.
questions.solution: 5x − 3 = 5x + 5. Subtract 5x: −3 = 5, which is false. No solution.

questions.hint: Simplify each side.
questions.solution: Left: 4x + 4. Right: 4x + 6 − 2 = 4x + 4. Both sides match, so all real numbers.

questions.hint: Multiply every term by 6.

questions.prompt: While solving, you reach 7 = 7. What does this mean?
questions.hint: The variable cancelled and the statement is true.
questions.solution: A true statement with no variable left means every real number works.

questions.hint: Simplify both sides first.

teach.title: Solving for a variable
text: A literal equation has several letters. To solve for one, treat the others like numbers and undo operations in reverse, just as you would with numbers.

questions.hint: h is multiplied by b. Undo with division.
questions.solution: Divide both sides by b: h = A/b.

questions.hint: Divide both sides by r.
questions.solution: t is multiplied by r. Divide by r: t = d/r.

questions.hint: Subtract 2w, then divide by 2.

questions.prompt: Solve y = mx + b for x.
questions.hint: Subtract b first, then divide by m.
questions.solution: y − b = mx, so x = (y − b)/m.

questions.prompt: A = lw. If A = 48 and w = 6, what is l?
questions.hint: Solve for l first: l = A/w.
r is multiplied by 2π.
questions.solution: Divide both sides by 2π: r = C/(2π).

questions.hint: P is multiplied by r and t.
questions.solution: Divide both sides by rt: P = I/(rt).

questions.prompt: d = rt. If d = 150 and r = 50, what is t?
questions.hint: t = d/r.

teach.title: Multi-step literal equations
text: Isolate the term with your variable, then undo what is attached to it. Move added or subtracted terms first. Then divide or multiply.
If you divide, divide every term on the other side.

questions.hint: Subtract 3x from both sides.
Divide every term by −5.

questions.prompt: Solve ax + b = c for x.
questions.hint: Subtract b, then divide by a.
questions.solution: ax = c − b, so x = (c − b)/a.

questions.hint: w is multiplied by l and h.
questions.solution: Divide both sides by lh: w = V/(lh).

questions.hint: Multiply both sides by b.
questions.solution: a/b = c, so a = bc.

questions.prompt: Solve x/m + n = p for x.
questions.hint: Subtract n, then multiply by m.
questions.solution: x/m = p − n, so x = m(p − n).

questions.prompt: Solve 4x + 3y = 24 for y, then find y when x = 3.
questions.hint: Subtract 4x from both sides, then divide by 3.
Multiply by 2, then divide by h.
questions.solution: 2A = bh, so b = 2A/h.

teach.title: Using a formula
text: Often it is easiest to substitute the numbers first, then solve. Or solve for the variable first and then substitute. Both give the same answer.
Always check that the answer makes sense for the situation.

example.problem: Use F = (9/5)C + 32 to find C when F = 50.

questions.hint: Subtract 32 first, then multiply by 5/9.

questions.prompt: A = (1/2)h(b₁ + b₂). A = 40, h = 5, b₁ = 6. Find b₂.
questions.hint: Substitute and solve.

questions.prompt: Simple interest: I = Prt. Find t if I = 90, P = 600, and r = 0.05.
questions.hint: Compute Pr first.

questions.prompt: P = 2l + 2w. If P = 50 and l = 15, find w.
questions.hint: Substitute, then solve.
Subtract 32 first, then multiply by 5/9.

questions.prompt: v = u + at. If v = 30, u = 6, and t = 4, find a.
questions.hint: Subtract u first.

questions.prompt: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁). If y = 11, y₁ = 3, x = 5, and x₁ = 1, find m.
questions.hint: Compute each difference first.
Subtract 2πr² and divide by 2πr.
questions.solution: S − 2πr² = 2πrh, so h = (S − 2πr²)/(2πr).

teach.title: Variable in more than one term
text: If your variable appears in two terms, collect those terms on one side and factor the variable out. Then divide.

example.problem: Solve A = P + Prt for P.
steps: Both terms contain P. Factor: A = P(1 + rt).

questions.prompt: Solve ax + bx = c for x.
questions.hint: Factor x out of the left side.
questions.solution: x(a + b) = c, so x = c/(a + b).

questions.hint: Distribute 3, then collect x terms.
questions.solution: 3x − 3a = 2x + b. Subtract 2x: x − 3a = b. Add 3a: x = b + 3a.

questions.prompt: Solve A = P + Prt for P.
questions.hint: Factor P out of both terms.
questions.solution: A = P(1 + rt), so P = A/(1 + rt).

questions.prompt: A = P(1 + rt). Find t if A = 1250, P = 1000, and r = 0.05.
questions.hint: Divide by P first.
Multiply by 2, then subtract a.
questions.solution: 2q = a + b, so b = 2q − a.

questions.prompt: (a + b)/2 = c. If a = 3 and c = 8, find b.
questions.hint: Multiply by 2 first.
Subtract x, then divide by −2.

questions.prompt: S = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh. If S = 62, w = 3, and h = 2, find l.
questions.hint: Put in w and h, then collect the l terms.

teach.title: Turning words into an equation
text: Pick a letter for the unknown number. Then translate each phrase in order.
"More than" and "plus" mean add. "Less than" means subtract from the other quantity. "Twice" and "times" mean multiply. "Is" means equals.

example.problem: Three more than twice a number is 17. Find the number.
steps: Twice the number is 2n. Three more than that is 2n + 3.

teach.title: Consecutive integers
text: Consecutive integers go up by 1: n, n + 1, n + 2.
Consecutive even integers or consecutive odd integers go up by 2: n, n + 2, n + 4.

example.problem: The sum of three consecutive integers is 72. Find them.
steps: Let the smallest be n. The others are n + 1 and n + 2.

questions.prompt: Which equation says "five less than three times a number is 22"?
questions.hint: Three times the number comes first. Then take away 5.
questions.solution: "Three times a number" is 3n. "Five less than" that is 3n − 5. So 3n − 5 = 22.

questions.prompt: Twice a number decreased by 6 equals 20. Find the number.
questions.hint: Write 2n − 6 = 20.

questions.prompt: Three consecutive integers start at n. Which expression is their sum?
questions.hint: Each integer is 1 more than the one before it.
questions.solution: The integers are n, n + 1, n + 2. Their sum is n + (n + 1) + (n + 2) = 3n + 3. Only that choice has the right terms.

questions.prompt: The sum of two consecutive integers is 85. What is the smaller one?
questions.hint: Call them n and n + 1.
questions.solution: n + (n + 1) = 85, so 2n + 1 = 85 and 2n = 84. n = 42. The integers are 42 and 43.

questions.prompt: The sum of three consecutive integers is 108. What is the smallest?
questions.solution: 3n + 3 = 108, so 3n = 105 and n = 35. The integers are 35, 36, 37, which add to 108. ✓

questions.prompt: Four consecutive integers add up to 138. What is the largest?
questions.hint: Use n, n + 1, n + 2, n + 3. Read the question again: you want the largest.

questions.prompt: Three consecutive even integers add up to 78. Which list is right?
questions.hint: Even integers go up by 2, so use n, n + 2, n + 4.
questions.solution: n + (n + 2) + (n + 4) = 78. 3n + 6 = 78, so n = 24. The integers are 24, 26, 28. The list 25, 26, 27 adds to 78 too, but those are not all even.

questions.prompt: The sum of three consecutive odd integers is 189. What is the smallest?
questions.hint: Odd integers go up by 2: n, n + 2, n + 4.

teach.title: Perimeter of a rectangle
text: Perimeter is the distance around: P = 2L + 2W.
When the length is described using the width, write the length in terms of the width first, then substitute.

example.problem: A rectangle is 4 cm longer than it is wide. Its perimeter is 44 cm. Find the width and length.
steps: Let w be the width. The length is w + 4.

teach.title: Triangles and other shapes
text: The perimeter of any polygon is the sum of its side lengths. Add the side expressions, combine like terms, and set the total equal to the perimeter.

example.problem: A triangle has sides x, x + 3, and 2x − 1. Its perimeter is 30. Find x.
steps: The sides are 7, 10, and 13. They add to 30. ✓

questions.prompt: A rectangle has width w and a length that is 5 more than the width. Which expression is its perimeter?
questions.hint: The perimeter uses two widths and two lengths.
questions.solution: Two widths give 2w. Two lengths give 2(w + 5). So P = 2w + 2(w + 5).

questions.prompt: A rectangle is 6 m longer than it is wide, and its perimeter is 52 m. What is the width in meters?
The length of a rectangle is twice its width. The perimeter is 60 ft. What is the length in feet?
questions.hint: If the width is w, the length is 2w. Then find w.

questions.prompt: A rectangle's length is 3 less than 4 times its width. The perimeter is 54 in. What is the width in inches?
questions.hint: Length = 4w − 3. Put that in the perimeter formula.

questions.prompt: A triangle has sides x, x + 5, and 2x − 3, and its perimeter is 38. What is the longest side?
questions.hint: Find x first. Then work out all three sides.
questions.solution: x + (x + 5) + (2x − 3) = 38. 4x + 2 = 38, so x = 9. The sides are 9, 14, and 15. The longest is 15.

questions.prompt: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides of 2x + 1 each, and a base of x + 4. The perimeter is 41. What is the base?
questions.hint: There are two equal sides, so add 2(2x + 1).
questions.solution: 2(2x + 1) + (x + 4) = 41. 4x + 2 + x + 4 = 41, so 5x + 6 = 41 and x = 7. The base is 7 + 4 = 11. The sides are 15, 15, 11, which add to 41. ✓

questions.prompt: A garden is 8 ft more than 3 times as long as it is wide. It needs 96 ft of fence around it. What are its dimensions?
questions.hint: Length = 3w + 8. Use P = 2w + 2(3w + 8). Remember to double the 8.

questions.prompt: A rectangle's perimeter is 70 cm and its length is 5 cm more than its width. What is its area in cm²?
questions.hint: Find the width and length first. Area = length × width.

teach.title: Quantity times price
text: For money problems, each group is worth (how many) × (price each). Add the groups to get the total.
If two groups add to a known total, call one group x and the other (total − x).

example.problem: A show sold 40 tickets. Adult tickets cost $8 and child tickets cost $5. Sales were $260. How many adult tickets were sold?
steps: Let a be the adult tickets. Child tickets are 40 − a.

teach.title: Flat fee plus a rate
text: Many costs are a fixed fee plus a rate times a number: total = fee + rate × amount.
To compare two plans, set their totals equal and solve.

example.problem: A gym charges a $25 sign-up fee plus $18 per month. How many months can you pay for with $187?

questions.prompt: Concert tickets cost $12 for adults and $7 for children. The venue sold 30 tickets, with x of them adult tickets. Which expression gives the total sales?
questions.hint: Children are what is left after the adults.
questions.solution: Adults: 12x dollars. Children: 30 − x tickets at $7, so 7(30 − x). Total: 12x + 7(30 − x).

questions.prompt: A taxi charges $3 plus $2 per mile. A ride costs $27. How many miles was it?
A streaming service charges a $9 sign-up fee and $12 each month. Kai has paid $93 in total. For how many months?
questions.hint: Fee + 12 × months = total.

questions.prompt: A jar has 25 coins, all nickels and dimes, worth $1.90. How many dimes are there?
questions.hint: Use cents: 5 per nickel, 10 per dime. If n is nickels, dimes are 25 − n.

questions.prompt: A school play sold 120 tickets. Student tickets were $5 and adult tickets were $8. Sales were $705. How many adult tickets were sold?
questions.hint: Let a be adult tickets. Students bought 120 − a.

questions.prompt: Dev has 14 bills, all $5 and $10 bills, worth $95. How many $10 bills does he have?
questions.hint: If f is the number of fives, tens are 14 − f.

questions.prompt: Plan A costs $30 to join plus $10 per month. Plan B has no joining fee and costs $15 per month. After how many months do the two plans cost the same?
questions.hint: Set the two total costs equal: 30 + 10m = 15m.
questions.solution: 30 + 10m = 15m. Subtract 10m: 30 = 5m. So m = 6. Both cost $90 after 6 months.

questions.prompt: Sam has $140 saved and adds $15 each week. Mia has $60 and adds $25 each week. After how many weeks do they have the same amount?
questions.hint: Set 140 + 15w equal to 60 + 25w.
questions.solution: 140 + 15w = 60 + 25w. Subtract 15w and 60: 80 = 10w, so w = 8. Each has $260. ✓

teach.title: Percent as a decimal
text: Change a percent to a decimal before you write the equation: 20% = 0.20, 7% = 0.07, 115% = 1.15.
A discount of 20% leaves 80% of the price, so the sale price is 0.80 times the original.
Always say what the unknown stands for. The unknown is usually the original amount.

example.problem: After a 20% discount, a jacket costs $64. What was the original price?
steps: Let x be the original price. After 20% off, you pay 80%.

teach.title: Tax, tips, and markups
text: Adding a percent to a price means you pay 100% + that percent. A 15% tip makes the total 1.15 times the bill.

example.problem: A meal plus a 15% tip costs $46. What was the meal price?
steps: Let x be the meal price. Total with tip is 1.15x.

questions.prompt: A shirt is 30% off. The sale price is $35. Which equation finds the original price x?
questions.hint: A 30% discount means you pay 70% of the original price.

questions.prompt: 25% of a number is 18. What is the number?
questions.hint: Write 0.25n = 18.

questions.prompt: After a 15% discount, a bike costs $51. What was its original price in dollars?
questions.hint: You pay 85% of the original: 0.85x = 51.

questions.prompt: A receipt shows $54 including 8% sales tax. What was the price before tax, in dollars?
questions.hint: Total = 1.08 times the price.

questions.prompt: Pete earns $12 per hour plus 6% of his sales. One week he worked 20 hours and earned $300. How many dollars of sales did he make?
questions.hint: Hourly pay is 12 × 20. The rest comes from commission.

questions.prompt: A town's population grew by 12% and is now 5600. What was it before the growth?
questions.hint: Now = 112% of before, so 1.12x = 5600.

questions.prompt: A store marks up the wholesale price by 40% to get a retail price of $84. What was the wholesale price?
questions.hint: Retail = 140% of wholesale.
questions.solution: 1.40x = 84, so x = 84 ÷ 1.40 = 60. Check: 40% of 60 is 24, and 60 + 24 = 84. ✓ The wholesale price was $60.

questions.prompt: Maya buys a laptop at 20% off, then pays 10% tax on the sale price. She pays $528 in total. What was the original price in dollars?
questions.hint: Total = 0.80 × 1.10 × original. Multiply the two decimals first.

teach.title: Solving like an equation, with one new rule
text: Solve an inequality the same way as an equation: undo adding and subtracting, then undo multiplying and dividing.
New rule: if you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number, flip the inequality sign.

steps: Divide by −3. The sign flips: x < −5.

teach.title: Graphing on a number line
text: A circle marks the endpoint. Use an open circle for < and >, because the number is not included. Use a closed circle for ≤ and ≥.
Shade the side where the solutions are. For x < 4, shade to the left of 4.

steps: Put a closed circle at 2, because 2 is included.
Shade to the right, toward the larger numbers.

questions.prompt: When do you reverse the direction of an inequality sign?
choices: When you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number
When you add a negative number to both sides
When the variable is on the right side
questions.hint: Think about what changes the order of numbers.
questions.solution: Adding or subtracting never changes the sign. Only multiplying or dividing by a negative does, because it reverses the order of numbers.

questions.hint: Subtract 7 from both sides.
questions.solution: x + 7 < 12. Subtract 7: x < 5.

questions.hint: Divide both sides by 4. It is positive, so the sign stays.
questions.solution: 4x ≥ 28. Divide by 4: x ≥ 7.

questions.hint: You divide by a negative number. What happens to the sign?
questions.solution: −2x ≤ 10. Divide by −2 and flip the sign: x ≥ −5.

questions.hint: Add 5 first, then divide.
questions.solution: 3x − 5 > 16. Add 5: 3x > 21. Divide by 3: x > 7.

questions.hint: Subtract 3, then divide by −4 and flip.
questions.solution: −4x + 3 ≥ 23. Subtract 3: −4x ≥ 20. Divide by −4 and flip the sign: x ≤ −5.

choices: Open circle at −2, shaded to the right
Closed circle at −2, shaded to the left
Closed circle at −2, shaded to the right
Open circle at −2, shaded to the left
questions.hint: Is −2 included? And is x bigger or smaller than −2?
questions.solution: ≥ includes −2, so the circle is closed. "Greater than" means shade to the right, toward larger numbers.

questions.hint: Subtract 7 from both sides first. Then divide by −2.
questions.solution: 7 − 2x < 1. Subtract 7: −2x < −6. Divide by −2 and flip: x > 3. Check x = 4: 7 − 8 = −1, and −1 < 1. ✓

teach.title: Variables on both sides
text: Move the variable terms to one side, as you do with equations. Keep the variable term positive if you can, so you do not have to flip.

teach.title: Distributing and fractions
text: Distribute first and combine like terms. To clear a fraction, multiply every term on both sides by the denominator. A positive multiplier does not flip the sign.

steps: Divide by −2 and flip the sign: x < −6.

questions.hint: Subtract 2x from both sides.
questions.solution: 6x + 1 > 2x + 17. Subtract 2x: 4x + 1 > 17. Subtract 1: 4x > 16. Divide by 4: x > 4.

questions.hint: Distribute the 3, or divide both sides by 3 first.
questions.solution: 3(x + 2) ≤ 21. Divide by 3: x + 2 ≤ 7. Subtract 2: x ≤ 5.

questions.hint: Subtract 8x from both sides. The x term becomes negative.
questions.solution: 5x − 8 ≥ 8x + 7. Subtract 8x: −3x − 8 ≥ 7. Add 8: −3x ≥ 15. Divide by −3 and flip: x ≤ −5.

questions.hint: Distribute, then collect the x terms on the left.
questions.solution: 6x − 2 < 4x + 10. Subtract 4x: 2x − 2 < 10. Add 2: 2x < 12. Divide by 2: x < 6.

questions.hint: Distribute the −3 carefully. You will divide by a negative at the end.
questions.solution: −3x + 12 > 2x − 8. Subtract 2x: −5x + 12 > −8. Subtract 12: −5x > −20. Divide by −5 and flip: x < 4.

questions.hint: Subtract 2 first. Then multiply by 3.
questions.solution: x/3 + 2 ≥ 5. Subtract 2: x/3 ≥ 3. Multiply by 3: x ≥ 9.

questions.hint: Multiply both sides by 3 first.
questions.solution: Multiply by 3: 2x − 1 < 15. Add 1: 2x < 16. Divide by 2: x < 8.

questions.hint: Subtract 4x from both sides and look at what is left.
questions.solution: Subtract 4x: 5 > −2. That is always true, so every real number is a solution.

teach.title: Interval notation
text: Interval notation writes the solution set as (left end, right end). Use ( ) when the end is not included or is infinite. Use [ ] when it is included.
Infinity always gets a parenthesis. x < 3 is (−∞, 3). x ≥ −1 is [−1, ∞).

example.problem: Solve 2x + 1 ≥ −5 and write the answer in interval notation.
steps: The −3 is included, so use a bracket: [−3, ∞).

teach.title: Reading a graph
text: An open circle matches a parenthesis. A closed circle matches a bracket. Shading to the right ends at ∞. Shading to the left starts at −∞.

example.problem: An open circle at 1 with shading to the left. What is the inequality and interval?
steps: Open circle at 1 means 1 is not included.
Shading to the left means smaller numbers: x < 1.

questions.hint: Greater than 4 goes up toward ∞. Is 4 included?
questions.solution: x > 4 does not include 4, so use a parenthesis. The values go up forever: (4, ∞).

questions.hint: Smaller numbers go toward −∞. Is −2 included?
questions.solution: x ≤ −2 includes −2, so use a bracket on that end. The values go down forever: (−∞, −2].

questions.prompt: Solve 3x + 2 < 11. Which interval is the solution?
questions.hint: Solve for x first. Then decide on brackets.
questions.solution: 3x + 2 < 11. Subtract 2: 3x < 9. Divide by 3: x < 3. Interval: (−∞, 3).

questions.prompt: Solve −5x ≤ 20. Which interval is the solution?
questions.hint: You divide by a negative number, so the sign flips.
questions.solution: −5x ≤ 20. Divide by −5 and flip: x ≥ −4. Interval: [−4, ∞).

questions.prompt: A graph has an open circle at 1 and shading to the right. Which inequality is it?
questions.hint: Open circle means the number is not included. Right means larger.
questions.solution: Open circle: not included, so the sign is strict. Shading right: larger numbers. The inequality is x > 1.

questions.prompt: Solve 2(x − 1) > 5x + 10. Which interval is the solution?
questions.hint: Distribute, collect x terms, then divide by a negative.
questions.solution: 2x − 2 > 5x + 10. Subtract 5x: −3x − 2 > 10. Add 2: −3x > 12. Divide by −3 and flip: x < −4. Interval: (−∞, −4).

questions.prompt: Solve 4 − (x − 3) ≥ 10. Which interval is the solution?
questions.hint: Subtracting a group changes both signs inside it.
questions.solution: 4 − x + 3 ≥ 10. Combine: 7 − x ≥ 10. Subtract 7: −x ≥ 3. Multiply by −1 and flip: x ≤ −3. Interval: (−∞, −3].

questions.prompt: What is the largest integer x that satisfies 3x − 4 < 20?
questions.hint: Solve the inequality. Then ask if 8 is allowed.
questions.solution: 3x − 4 < 20. Add 4: 3x < 24. Divide by 3: x < 8. The number 8 is not included, so the largest integer is 7.

teach.title: Key phrases
text: "At least" means ≥. "At most" and "no more than" mean ≤. "More than" means >. "Fewer than" and "less than" mean <.
Define the variable, write the inequality, solve, and then say what the answer means.

example.problem: A truck rental costs $40 plus $0.25 per mile. Your budget is at most $100. How many miles can you drive?
steps: Let m be the miles. Cost: 40 + 0.25m.
Divide by 0.25: m ≤ 240. You can drive up to 240 miles.

teach.title: Making sense of the answer
text: If the variable counts whole things, such as tickets or tests, choose a whole number that fits the inequality. For x > 7.5 the smallest whole number is 8.

example.problem: You need more than 7.5 hours. What is the smallest whole number of hours?
steps: Hours must be whole here, and 7 is too small.

questions.prompt: Which symbol goes with the words "at least"?
questions.hint: At least means that number or more.
questions.solution: "At least 5" means 5 or more, so x ≥ 5.

questions.prompt: Twice a number plus 3 is at most 21. Which inequality models this?
questions.hint: "At most" means no bigger than. Twice the number is 2n.
questions.solution: "Twice a number plus 3" is 2n + 3. "At most 21" means ≤ 21.

questions.prompt: What is the largest integer n with 2n + 3 ≤ 21?
questions.hint: Solve the inequality first.
questions.solution: 2n + 3 ≤ 21. Subtract 3: 2n ≤ 18. Divide by 2: n ≤ 9. The largest integer is 9.

questions.prompt: A phone plan costs $20 plus $0.10 per text. The budget is at most $45. What is the most texts you can send?
questions.solution: 20 + 0.10t ≤ 45. Subtract 20: 0.10t ≤ 25. Divide by 0.10: t ≤ 250. You can send at most 250 texts.

questions.prompt: Lena needs an average of at least 80 over 4 tests. Her first three scores are 72, 85, and 78. What is the lowest fourth score that works?
questions.hint: The four scores must total at least 4 × 80.
questions.solution: The total must be at least 320. The first three add to 235. So 235 + x ≥ 320, and x ≥ 85. The lowest score is 85.

questions.prompt: A club sells tickets for $6 each. Its fixed cost is $150. What is the fewest tickets it must sell to make a profit of more than $300?
questions.hint: Profit = 6t − 150. "More than" is strict.
questions.solution: 6t − 150 > 300. Add 150: 6t > 450. Divide by 6: t > 75. Since it must be strictly more than 75, the fewest whole number is 76.

questions.prompt: Gym A costs $50 to join plus $20 per month. Gym B costs $30 per month with no joining fee. When is Gym A cheaper?
questions.hint: Write 50 + 20m < 30m and solve.
questions.solution: 50 + 20m < 30m. Subtract 20m: 50 < 10m. So m > 5. Gym A is cheaper after more than 5 months.

questions.prompt: A rectangle is 12 cm long. Its perimeter must be less than 50 cm. What is the largest whole-number width in centimeters?
questions.hint: Perimeter: 2(12) + 2w < 50.
questions.solution: 24 + 2w < 50. Subtract 24: 2w < 26. Divide by 2: w < 13. The largest whole number is 12.

teach.title: "And" means both
text: A compound inequality joins two inequalities. With "and", a number must make both true. The solutions are where the two graphs overlap, which is a segment between two ends.
You can write "x > 2 and x < 7" as 2 < x < 7.

steps: Do the same step to all three parts. Subtract 3: −2 < 2x < 6.

teach.title: Reading and graphing
text: On a number line, shade between the two endpoints. Use an open circle for < and a closed circle for ≤, one for each end.

steps: The ends −1 and 3 are not included.
The integers between them are 0, 1, and 2.

questions.prompt: Which inequality means the same as "x > 2 and x < 7"?
questions.hint: "And" keeps only the numbers that fit both parts.
questions.solution: Numbers greater than 2 and less than 7 lie between 2 and 7. That is 2 < x < 7.

questions.prompt: Which number is a solution of −3 < x ≤ 4?
questions.hint: Test each number against both ends.
questions.solution: 0 is between −3 and 4, so it works. −3 is not included. 5 and −4 are outside.

questions.prompt: A graph has a closed circle at −1, an open circle at 5, and shading between them. Which inequality is it?
questions.hint: Closed circle means ≤. Open circle means <.
questions.solution: The left end −1 is closed, so −1 ≤ x. The right end 5 is open, so x < 5. Together: −1 ≤ x < 5.

questions.hint: Subtract 1 from all three parts.
questions.solution: Subtract 1 from every part: 3 − 1 < x < 8 − 1. So 2 < x < 7.

questions.hint: Divide all three parts by 2.
questions.solution: Divide every part by 2: −2 ≤ x < 5.

questions.hint: List them. Is −2 included? Is 5?
questions.solution: The integers are −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. That is 7 integers.

questions.hint: Add 1 to all three parts first. Then divide by 3.
questions.solution: Add 1: −6 < 3x < 9. Divide by 3: −2 < x < 3.

questions.prompt: What is the largest integer that satisfies 5 < 2x + 1 < 15?
questions.hint: Solve for x first. Then check whether the right end is included.
questions.solution: Subtract 1: 4 < 2x < 14. Divide by 2: 2 < x < 7. The number 7 is not included, so the largest integer is 6.

teach.title: "Or" means either
text: With "or", a number only has to make one of the inequalities true. The graph is both shaded pieces together. The pieces usually point away from each other.
Solve each part separately. Do not combine them into one chain.

teach.title: When "or" overlaps
text: If the two shaded pieces overlap or touch, they cover the whole line, so the answer is all real numbers.

steps: Every number is either at most 5 or more than 1. A number like 3 is both.
Together they cover everything: all real numbers, (−∞, ∞).

questions.prompt: Which graph shows x < −2 or x ≥ 3?
choices: Open circle at −2 shaded left, closed circle at 3 shaded right
Open circle at −2 and closed circle at 3, shaded between them
Closed circle at −2 shaded left, open circle at 3 shaded right
Open circle at −2 shaded right, closed circle at 3 shaded left
questions.hint: "Or" gives two pieces, pointing away from each other.
questions.solution: x < −2 is an open circle at −2 with shading left. x ≥ 3 is a closed circle at 3 with shading right.

questions.hint: Solve each inequality on its own.
questions.solution: x + 3 < 1 gives x < −2. x − 2 > 5 gives x > 7. The answer is x < −2 or x > 7.

questions.hint: Divide 2x ≤ −6 by 2. Positive, so no flip.
questions.solution: 2x ≤ −6 gives x ≤ −3. The second part is already x > 1. The answer is x ≤ −3 or x > 1.

questions.prompt: Write x ≤ −3 or x > 1 in interval notation.
questions.hint: Closed circle: bracket. Open circle: parenthesis.
questions.solution: x ≤ −3 is (−∞, −3] and x > 1 is (1, ∞). Join them with ∪.

questions.hint: Dividing by −2 flips the sign.
questions.solution: 3x − 1 ≥ 8 gives 3x ≥ 9, so x ≥ 3. −2x > 4 gives x < −2. The answer is x ≥ 3 or x < −2.

questions.prompt: How many integers from −5 to 5 (both included) satisfy x < −3 or x ≥ 2?
questions.hint: List the integers from each piece. Do not count one twice.
questions.solution: x < −3 gives −5 and −4. x ≥ 2 gives 2, 3, 4, 5. That is 2 + 4 = 6 integers.

questions.hint: In the first one, you divide by −1 at the end and flip.
questions.solution: 5 − x < 1: subtract 5 to get −x < −4, so x > 4. 2x + 3 < −5: 2x < −8, so x < −4. The answer is x < −4 or x > 4.

questions.hint: Solve each part, then see whether the pieces overlap.
questions.solution: x − 1 ≤ 4 gives x ≤ 5. x + 2 > 3 gives x > 1. Every number is at most 5 or more than 1, so the answer is all real numbers.

teach.title: No solution
text: With "and", if the two pieces do not overlap, no number works. The answer is no solution (the empty set).
Check: x > 6 and x < 1 would need a number above 6 and below 1 at once. That cannot happen.

steps: No number is greater than 4 and less than −2, so there is no solution.

teach.title: All real numbers
text: With "or", if the two pieces cover the whole number line, the answer is all real numbers, written (−∞, ∞).
For a chain a < expression < b, do the same step on all three parts. The interval notation is (a, b) with brackets where "or equal to" appears.

questions.hint: Is there a number above 6 that is also below 1?
questions.solution: No number is both greater than 6 and less than 1. So there is no solution.

questions.hint: Try a few numbers, such as 0, 2, and 5.
questions.solution: Any number is either less than 4 or greater than 1. Numbers like 2 are both. So all real numbers work.

questions.hint: Solve each part. Then look for an overlap.
questions.solution: 2x + 1 > 9 gives x > 4. x − 3 < −5 gives x < −2. They do not overlap, so there is no solution.

questions.hint: Solve each part. Do the pieces overlap?
questions.solution: 3x − 2 ≤ 7 gives x ≤ 3. x + 5 ≥ 2 gives x ≥ −3. The pieces overlap, so every number works: all real numbers.

questions.prompt: Solve 4 < 2x − 2 ≤ 10. Which interval is the solution?
questions.hint: Add 2 to all three parts. Then divide by 2.
questions.solution: Add 2: 6 < 2x ≤ 12. Divide by 2: 3 < x ≤ 6. The left end is open and the right end is closed: (3, 6].

questions.prompt: Solve −9 ≤ 3x − 3 < 6. Which interval is the solution?
questions.hint: Add 3 to every part first.
questions.solution: Add 3: −6 ≤ 3x < 9. Divide by 3: −2 ≤ x < 3. Interval: [−2, 3).

questions.prompt: What is the sum of all the integers that satisfy −2 ≤ x < 3?
questions.hint: List the integers. Is 3 included?
questions.solution: The integers are −2, −1, 0, 1, 2. Their sum is −2 + −1 + 0 + 1 + 2 = 0.

questions.prompt: Which compound inequality has no solution?
questions.hint: Look for the one where the two pieces cannot overlap and both must be true.
questions.solution: "x > 3 and x < −1" needs a number above 3 and below −1 at the same time. That is impossible. The others have solutions.

teach.title: Translating words
text: "Between" with no extra words means the ends are not included: 20 < t < 28. "At least … and at most …" includes the ends: 70 ≤ s ≤ 90.
"Or" situations, like a discount for kids under 12 or adults over 65, use two separate pieces.

example.problem: A pool is safe when its temperature T is at least 26° and at most 30°. Write an inequality.

teach.title: Solve, then answer the question
text: Write the compound inequality, solve it, and read what it says about the situation. Whole-number answers need a final check at each end.

example.problem: A taxi charges $4 plus $2 per mile. You want to spend between $10 and $20, ends included. How many miles?
steps: You can go from 3 to 8 miles.

questions.prompt: A score s must be at least 70 and at most 90. Which inequality is that?
questions.hint: "At least" and "at most" include the ends.
questions.solution: At least 70 is s ≥ 70, and at most 90 is s ≤ 90. Together: 70 ≤ s ≤ 90.

questions.prompt: Water must be strictly between 20 °C and 28 °C. Which inequality is that?
questions.hint: "Strictly between" does not include the ends.
questions.solution: Strictly between 20 and 28 means more than 20 and less than 28: 20 < t < 28.

questions.prompt: A plan costs $15 plus $5 per hour. The total must be between $40 and $65, ends included. Which compound inequality models the hours h?
questions.hint: The total cost is 15 + 5h. It must stay inside the range.
questions.solution: The total cost is 15 + 5h. It must be at least 40 and at most 65, so 40 ≤ 15 + 5h ≤ 65.

questions.prompt: Using the plan above, 40 ≤ 15 + 5h ≤ 65, what is the most hours you can use?
questions.hint: Subtract 15 from all three parts. Then divide by 5.
questions.solution: Subtract 15: 25 ≤ 5h ≤ 50. Divide by 5: 5 ≤ h ≤ 10. The most is 10 hours.

questions.prompt: Skis rent for $12 plus $4 per hour. Joan wants to pay more than $20 and at most $36. How many different whole numbers of hours could she rent for?
questions.hint: Write 20 < 12 + 4h ≤ 36 and solve. Then list the whole numbers.
questions.solution: Subtract 12: 8 < 4h ≤ 24. Divide by 4: 2 < h ≤ 6. The whole numbers are 3, 4, 5, 6. That is 4 values.

questions.prompt: A museum gives a discount to anyone under 12 or 65 and older. Which describes the ages a that get the discount?
questions.hint: This is "or": two separate pieces.
questions.solution: Under 12 is a < 12. 65 and older is a ≥ 65. A person is in one group or the other, so use "or".

questions.hint: Multiply all three parts by 2, then add 1.
questions.solution: Multiply by 2: −10 < x − 1 < 6. Add 1: −9 < x < 7. Interval: (−9, 7).

questions.prompt: How many integers satisfy both 2x − 1 ≤ 7 and 3x + 2 > −4?
questions.hint: Solve each inequality. Then find the overlap.
questions.solution: 2x − 1 ≤ 7 gives x ≤ 4. 3x + 2 > −4 gives 3x > −6, so x > −2. The solutions are −2 < x ≤ 4. The integers are −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. That is 6.

teach.title: Absolute value means distance
